deadline.value: The 2026-27 SciDoc rounds close 16 November 2026, 25 January 2027 and 15 April 2027; the earliest is listed here.
deadline.quote: Academic year 2026-2027 application periods: | 3-16 November 2026 | 12-25 January 2027 | 2-15 April 2027

gre_subject.value: The SciDoc pages do not mention a GRE Subject test.

supervisor.value: Each applicant needs a main supervisor and a coordinating academic, and a signed supervision agreement must be submitted with the application.
supervisor.quote: Each applicant must have at minimum, a main supervisor and a coordinating academic | Applications lacking a signed supervision agreement will not proceed to academic evaluation

funding.value: Applicants must present a realistic funding plan, with secured funding normally required for the first year; the page does not say admitted students are funded.
funding.quote: Secured funding is normally required for at least the first year of full-time doctoral studies

also.quote: Call for applications for new university-funded doctoral researcher positions is opened once a year

entry_route.value: Applicants must hold a second-cycle (master's-level) degree or equivalent; the page offers no direct route from a bachelor's degree.
entry_route.quote: Applicants to the Doctoral Programme in Science (SciDoc) must have completed: | An applicable second-cycle university degree

notes: One umbrella programme, Doctoral Programme in Science (SciDoc), covers seven discipline areas: atmospheric and climate-system sciences, chemistry, computer science, geosciences and geography, materials and nanoscience, mathematics and statistics, and particle physics and universe sciences. The Faculty of Science is the target faculty for physics, astronomy and chemistry. Data science is only a topic inside computer science. The 'Academic year 2026-2027 application periods' list gives the three 2027 rounds; the start dates for those rounds are not published.
